I tested the Xreal Aura glasses for 2 weeks — amazing displays and immersive spatial computing let down by a lack of apps

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xreal and Google's first foray into XR glasses is a fascinating look at the future of AR and VR devices.
  • It has been revealed that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you.
  • For quite awhile I have firmly believed that smart glasses are the next device that will evolve the future of computing, much like the iPhone heralded the next 20 years of tech progression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xreal and Google's first foray into XR glasses is a fascinating look at the future of AR and VR devices. But that also means you're prototyping something that will get better, but maybe not yet.

It has been revealed that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

For quite awhile I have firmly believed that smart glasses are the next device that will evolve the future of computing, much like the iPhone heralded the next 20 years of tech progression. And this is despite the current "pervert glasses" backlash.

In a recent development, I am fascinated by the sudden influx of AR and XR glasses that offer immersive environments and while also looking "normal." I've already tried Meta VR Glasses and Snap Specs, but neither are actually available for everyone yet. The Google, Qualcomm and Xreal collaboration Aura glasses are.

All three glasses could be considered VR-lite, but I think they're about finding a use between AI glasses and wearing a full headset.

Sources indicate that in that way, the Auras are the escaped experiment worth investigating. Following the Samsung Galaxy XR headset, these are just the second device to run Google's Android XR platform natively.

This first stab at an XR headset that I think most people will want is impressive and a great example of what Android XR could be, but it also means you're the guinea pig with all that implies.

90g (glasses)265g (compute puck).

Xreal S1 andQualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform.

Sources indicate that right when the Aura rolled out on November 17, I put together some early impressions of the glassese. For the most part, my thoughts haven't changed. But after using the glasses more, some plusses and minuses have solidified.

I am not an advocate for VR as it currently works with bulky, isolating headsets. However, I can still be impressed virtual reality experiences.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sources indicate that the Xreal Aura provides that with 6DoF spatial computing. The two temple cameras and the nose bridge camera enable pinch gesture controls and you can always use the puck as trackpad, which I defaulted to more often that not.

Recent findings suggest that the pinch controls work well. Occasionally the hitbox was a hair off but I didn't notice lag when I adjusted. I will note that in darker environments, it didn't always work, which isn't totally surprising but something to know.

Out of the box, the Auras come with a variety of mixed-reality experiences, from a VR tour of the Galapagos, to some games and a 360 version of Google Maps that is a delight to explore.

According to recent reports, VR enthusiasts will find the 70-degree field of view limiting but I wasn't bothered by it. Watching movies feels like you're in a theater for yourself, and extending my desktop workspace was seamless via the wired accessory cable (or wireless for some devices).

These might be the best displays Xreal has made to date. I tested the refreshed Xreal One Pro Plus a couple of weeks ago and thought it was an improvement, and now the Aura is taking it even further.

Industry observers note that xreal lists the resolution of the Aura's as 1,920 x 1,200 per eye (1200p). It makes for sharp images, especially in games and media. It feels premium.

The color gamut isn't robust and the Aura doesn't offer HDR like the One Pro Plus, but if you don't need that level of display detail, these look good. Plus, with 1200 nits of brightness, the display can handle a number of settings. And the electrochromic dimming gets pretty dark, meaning you should feel more immersed.

Personally, I have never had great luck reading text as is on AR glasses, and while the Aura's are better, you may find text blurry. Fortunately, you can zoom in, which helps.

One advantage the Xreal Aura glasses have over Meta's VR Glasses and the Snap Specs is the built-in Google ecosystem. Snap and Meta have both promised that they're building up their developer connections to create more apps for their glasses, but Google's slew of in-house designs and third-party apps is already robust.

Sources indicate that on the productivity side, you've got the entire Google suite from Docs and Drive to your calendar and Gmail. Plus, there's the Google Play Store with normal phone games and a small but growing number of XR-specific apps.

Moving forward, as Android XR grows, this will be what sets the Aura and future Android XR devices apart from Snap and Meta.

Recent findings suggest that here's the rub: you don't really need XR glasses yet. Xreal's own lineup of AR glasses are already great for productivity, gaming and watching content by connecting to your laptop, mini PC, phone or gaming device.

Because of that, the flaws do stand out a bit more.

If we're thinking of the Aura as VR-lite, especially compared to the Meta VR Glasses, then the biggest missing component for the Xreal Aura glasses is games.

Yes, I did try Demeo, which was fun, and HoloChess, which felt like the Star Wars version of chess. But from what I could tell, there aren't many native XR/VR games on the Play Store, while the Meta Quest Store has hundreds, and Meta promised at least 75 launch titles specifically designed for the VR glasses next year.

You can play 2D games on the Play Store, which I did with some games I already have on my account. Xreal is selling its own first-party controller made with GameSir, but you can use any Bluetooth controller. Again, you can connect other Xreal glasses to your phone, laptop, or gaming device with a controller as well.

It's not clear how long it'll take native Android XR experiences to catch up to Meta, but for now, Meta has the lead.

According to recent reports, xreal rates the battery life of the Aura puck between three and four hours. I found that to be pretty accurate. In my testing watching an hour-long YouTube video and then playing some games for about 20 minutes knocked the battery life from 100% to about 80%.

In a recent development, I debated putting this as a flaw because I'm not sure if you want to keep these glasses on for more than three hours. Perhaps that is the sweet spot. Still, for anything longer, you'll need to recharge.

That mentioned, heat becomes a concern. The puck can get warm, but it does include a fan to dissipate heat. Surprisingly, the glasses can get quite warm, especially in the area that runs across your forehead.

Industry observers note that general use seemed okay, but at one point I accidentally turned on screen recording and I could feel the glasses heating up. It never got laptop-panini levels of hot, but as the tech ages, I foresee this being a problem.

The Xreal Auras have just three cameras. Two on the temples and one on the nose bridge. As mentioned, I find the hand tracking pretty decent and pinch gestures work well.

However, I've also worn the Meta VR Glasses, which have 6 external cameras and four internal ones. Fundamentally, Xreal adding seven more cameras would change the design of the glasses, which you can see in the ski-goggle look of Meta's forthcoming platform.

According to recent reports, still, eye tracking makes navigating the XR space better. And compared to Meta, where you can leave your hand on the table or in your lap and still use gesture controls, the three-camera Aura setup is more limiting.

The pushback is the puck trackpad, which I used most frequently. I am comfortable with trackpads and mice, and the puck is a nice midway point.

The puck is a mini-PC with glasses attached, but that doesn't make navigation the best without accessories or the trackpad.

If Xreal's next iteration can add eye tracking or even a couple more external cameras, the already good hand tracking would be even better.

According to recent reports, I find the Xreal Aura glasses fascinating, and when its rivals finally launch, I think a latest space in the tech world will open up that is more than just pervert glasses and bulky headsets. Perhaps I've given these glasses more grace than future versions will deserve, but for a first go in this space, I'm excited by the potential.

For many, I'm not sure the $1,000+ price tag is cheap enough to dive in, but for the curious and the early adopters, this is a device of potential. It hints at what mixed reality wearables could be.

When I use the Aura, I get what it's supposed to be. It's the taste of a Vision Pro or Quest headset in a lighter, more comfortable package. Xreal has set the bar; it'll be up to everyone to see if they can raise it.

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, at the moment the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was launched the same month, with the company describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Recent findings suggest that muse initially launched as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It quickly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

Industry observers note that it wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I said at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

“This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post.

Industry observers note that the report says this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

Industry observers note that “I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Patch: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

In a recent development, "AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

It has been revealed that the instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

It has been revealed that meta has taken glitch with the messaging claims. It says that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

It has been revealed that with Android, customers have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The company also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, presently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever.   • Canva today unveiled upcoming controls that will let Free and Pro owners choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from users who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing new settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today unveiled upcoming controls that will let Free and Pro owners choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The manufacturer notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company states that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between owners with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two fresh controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the company noted that select features that use AI without generating upcoming content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

“Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the organization’s design content library, Canva said that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

Industry News: If You Loved 'Phony,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us.
  • Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).
  • A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar shows) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

In a recent development, the boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

According to recent reports, the Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a latest employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, on one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

Latest Update: 10 Artists Who Should Perform The Next James Bond

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With Robert Pattinson set to play James Bond, the next big question, outside who will play the female lead, is what artist will sing the theme for his 007 debut.
  • In a recent development, three 007 debuts came with a jolt of rock energy; Roger Moore's made his entrance to Paul McCartney & Wings' explosive "Live and Let Die," Timothy Dalton arrived to Aha's synth-driven "The Living Daylights," and Daniel Craig's Casino Royale opened with Chris Cornell's hard-rocker "You Know My Name." The history give producers plenty of reason to consider another rock theme for Pattinson's debut.
  • It has been revealed that oasis returned with authority in 2025 with a sold-out stadium tour that drew crowds of beer-drinking, Adidas-clad fans around the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With Robert Pattinson set to play James Bond, the next big question, outside who will play the female lead, is what artist will sing the theme for his 007 debut. The franchise has drawn some of music's biggest names, from Shirley Bassey and Tom Jones to Madonna, Adele, Sam Smith, and Billie Eilish. The theme songs range from brassy orchestral showpieces and jazz-inflected sweeping pop ballads and full-throttle rock anthems, leaving plenty of room for the next artist to put their stamp on a Bond theme.

In a recent development, three 007 debuts came with a jolt of rock energy; Roger Moore's made his entrance to Paul McCartney & Wings' explosive "Live and Let Die," Timothy Dalton arrived to Aha's synth-driven "The Living Daylights," and Daniel Craig's Casino Royale opened with Chris Cornell's hard-rocker "You Know My Name." The history give producers plenty of reason to consider another rock theme for Pattinson's debut. Here are 10 artists who should record the next Bond theme, ranked from the least obvious to the strongest fit.

It has been revealed that oasis returned with authority in 2025 with a sold-out stadium tour that drew crowds of beer-drinking, Adidas-clad fans around the world. The Manchester band's loud guitars and defiant attitude are made for stadium sing-a-longs, from "Champagne Supernova," and "Don't Look Back in Anger," to "Wonderwall." Two deeper cuts make a strong case for Bond. "Let's All Make Believe" and "Falling Down" are two cinematic songs that show how Oasis could bring both muscle and menace to a rock-driven theme.

Industry observers note that the group sounds like a great fit on paper, but persuading the Gallagher brothers to write and record an original theme may be a tough sell. The success of their reunion showed the world still has an appetite for Oasis, whose last studio album, Dig Out Your Soul, came out in 2008. Asking the famously cantankerous brother to make their studio comeback on the movie's production schedule would be a huge gamble for Amazon MGM, who seem to be playing it safe. That makes Oasis one of the least likely entries on this list.

Fred Again.., born Frederick John Phillip Gibson, is one of electronic dance music's most unique producers. The English DJ and producer started out playing classical piano and percussion, and his connection to Bond goes back to the very first 007 novel. His great-grandmother, Ann Charteris, married Bond creator Ian Fleming in March 1952, a year before Casino Royale introduced James Bond to readers. That makes Fleming Gibson's step-great-grandfather.

Sources indicate that gibson broke through during the COVID-19 pandemic, turning voice notes, phone videos and social media clips into the emotional center of his tracks. On his 2021 hit "Marea (we've lost dancing)," he set a lockdown conversation with Marea Stamper, better known as The Blessed Madonna, to a dance beat. The track captured how much people missed the simple act of congregating together on dance floors, while giving them something to groove to in the meantime. He indicated his harder edge on "Rumble," a grimy dubstep collaboration with Skrillex and UK rapper Flowdan that won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Recording. "Jungle" is another banger loaded with menacing sounds like a Tiger growl and the metallic click of a gun being cocked cutting through the pulsating bass. "Enough," from his 2023 collaboration with Brian Eno, shows how much tension Gibson can create with little more than a voice and hazy ambient sounds. Fred Again.. would also be a natural choice to give an electronic twist to the original "James Bond Theme," composed by Monty Norman and arranged by John Barry.

According to recent reports, dua Lipa has a string of dance-pop radio hits, including "Training Season," "Newly introduced Rules," "One Kiss," "Levitating," and "Dance the Night." The London-born singer scored two chart-topping albums in the UK with 2020's Future Nostalgia and 2024's Radical Optimism, and her three Grammy wins include Best New Artist and Best Pop Vocal Album for Future Nostalgia. The string sample on "Love Again" gives its disco groove a touch of old-school glamour, while the pulsating synths on "Houdini," co-written and co-produced by Tame Impala's Kevin Parker, suggest a more urgent, dance-driven Bond theme. "Homesick," the piano ballad she co-wrote with Coldplay's Chris Martin, makes the case for a slower approach that will allow her understated delivery to give the song the emotional weight to carry a sweeping 007 ballad.

In a recent development, dua Lipa already has a close connection to the Bond casting race. Her husband, Callum Turner, was in the running to play Bond before Robert Pattinson landed the role. It's fun to imagine Turner making his Bond debut with Lipa singing over the opening credits. She'd be a strong choice for Pattinson's debut, too. With her grand pop hooks, dance grooves and enormous confidence, Dua Lipa would give the upcoming Bond an electrifying opening theme.

Industry observers note that arctic Monkeys formed in Sheffield, England in 2002 and made their name with quirky guitar riffs, a powerful rhythm section with frontman Alex Turner's sharp observations and quick, conversational vocal delivery. Their 2006 debut, Whatever You Say I Am, That's What I'm Not, became the fastest-selling debut album in UK chart history at the time, and began a run of six straight UK number one studio LPs. The quartet's sound evolved from the frantic indie rock of "I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor," to the slinky, blues-driven riffs of "Do I Wanna Know?" and "R U Mine?," and the late-night ballad "No. 1 Party Anthem.".

Sources indicate that alex Turner's deep, soulful croon, drenched in his Sheffield accent, has a warmth and quiet confidence suited to a throwback Bond theme. The soaring strings of "There'd Better Be a Mirrorball" and the slow build of "Body Paint" show how naturally Arctic Monkeys could handle an orchestral ballad, while the ominous synth beneath "Sculptures of Anything Goes" gives shades of a dark underbelly that is equally intriguing. The band famously covered Shirley Bassey's "Diamonds are Forever" during their 2007 Glastonbury headlining set, and Turner told NME in 2011 that he would "love to do a tune for Bond." An Arctic Monkey theme would give Pattinson's 007 an opening with elegance, mystery and just the right amount swagger.

It has been revealed that muse formed in Devon, England, in 1994 and built their sound around distorted bass, heavy guitar riffs, classical piano and Matt Bellamy's soaring vocals. The trio's flair for drama runs through songs like "Uprising," "Resistance," "Madness, "Dead Inside," and "Thought Contagion." Muse have scored eight consecutive UK number one studio albums, from 2003's Absolution to 2026's The Wow! Signal. They won the Grammy for Best Rock Album in 2011 for The Resistance and again in 2016 for Drones.

It has been revealed that the group's 2012 track "Supremacy" is a cinematic song that pairs a heavy guitar riff with Matt Bellamy's hushed verses and dramatic orchestration that eerily resembles a Bond theme, complete with an arpeggiated guitar chord at the end. Muse already has a connection with Robert Pattinson through the first three Twilight films, from "Supermassive Black Hole" in the original soundtrack and "Neutron Star Collision (Love Is Forever)" for Eclipse. Bellamy also co-wrote the end-title music for the 2009 thriller The International. The band's theatrical, arena rock sound and classical influences would bring a bombastic energy to the Bond theme.

Lana Del Rey already has a lot of history with 007. She wrote "24" for Spectre, but producers chose Sam Smith's sweeping ballad "Writings on the Wall" for the 2015 film. She included the track featuring her soft and smoky vocals on her 2015 album Honeymoon. The vocalist also co-wrote and recorded "First Light" with longtime Bond composer David Arnold for the 2026 video game 007 First Light. She's already written two songs for Bond. The next step would be finally hearing one over the opening credits.

Industry observers note that del Rey's catalog makes a strong case for a Bond title sequence. "Shades of Cool," and "Honeymoon" have the slow-burning tension of classic 007 themes, while "Young and Beautiful" and "Born to Die" show how naturally her intimate voice carries over an orchestra. Her ability to blend romance and danger makes her a great fit for a Bond theme.

Radiohead have their own lengthy history with 007. Like Lana Del Rey, the British rockers recorded a song for Spectre, but producers went with Sam Smith's "Writings on the Wall." Radiohead released their rejected theme, "Spectre," on Christmas Day 2015. The brooding ballad opens with a sparse piano and Thom Yorke's fragile vocals before rising strings and the band joins in to bring the song to an orchestral climax.

Long before "Spectre," Radiohead covered Carly Simon's "Nobody Does It Better" the theme from 1977's The Spy Who Loved Me. Around the same time, they also wrote and recorded "Man of War" as a nod to Bond music. The band submitted it for Spectre, but producers passed again, and the band finally released it on OKNOTOK, the 20th anniversary edition of OK Computer. Both "Spectre" and "Man of War" are clear examples of how Radiohead could take a Bond title sequence in different directions.

Olivia Dean was born in North London and honed her craft at the Brit School. The singer-songwriter plays piano and guitar, paring R&B grooves with her warm and sultry voice. She scored two UK number one singles, "Rein Me In," her duet with Sam Fender, and "Man I Need," which reached number two in the US, spending 57 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

Dean won the 2026 Grammy for Best Latest Artist and is up for six awards at the 2027 ceremony, including Record, Song and Album of the Year. "Loud" has the hallmarks of a classic Bond ballad, while "Danger" has a reggae lift with a modern sound. She recorded "It Isn't Perfect But It Might Be" for 2025's Bridget Jones: Mad About the Boy, showing how comfortably she can carry a film ballad. Dean's jazz-influenced phrasing and ear for a pop hook would give 007 a theme with the warmth of classic soul.

Harry Styles is a strong candidate to sing the next James Bond theme. His 2017 debut solo single "Sign of the Times" builds from a spare piano to a soaring rock climax, proving he can deliver a Bond-worthy theme. Style's 2026 epic "Coming Up Roses" features a 39-piece orchestra that heightens the tension around his intimate vocals. The combination of his unpredictability, vulnerability and the grandeur of his music would be a fitting cinematic theme for Robert Pattinson's 007.

Styles, who made his acting debut in Christopher Nolan's 2017 movie Dunkirk, was once rumored to be in the running to play James Bond. His representative dismissed reports in 2020 that he was in line to succeed Daniel Craig. As a singer, Styles would be a natural fit for a slow-burning theme in the vein of Adele's "Skyfall," with an arrangement that draws on the orchestral legacy of Shirley Bassey's trio of "Diamonds are Forever," "Moonraker," and "Goldfinger.".

Sources indicate that RAYE was born Rachel Agatha Keen in South London. She attended the BRIT School, as did Olivia Dean, Adele and the late Amy Winehouse. She signed a record deal at 17 and made her name singing dance tracks, while writing for Beyonce and Little Mix. Her second album, 2026's This Music May Contain Hope, features "Where Is My Husband," which topped the UK Singles Chart and peaked at number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100. RAYE leads the 2027 Grammy field with 11 nominations, including Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Album of the Year and Songwriter of the Year, Non-classical.

It has been revealed that the singer has already worked with Hans Zimmer, who scored No Time to Die. They collaborated on "Mother Nature" and "Click Clack Symphony" for the 2023 BBC documentary series Planet Earth III. Both songs are exemplary showcases for a sweeping 007 arrangement. "Oscar Winning Tears" brings that same scale to R&B, while "The Thrill is Gone" shows off the bluesy attitude she would bring to the franchise. At the 2025 Oscars, RAYE closed the Bond tribute medley with "Skyfall" after LISA's "Live and Let Die" and Doja Cat's "Diamonds Are Forever." Her soulful voice along with big brass arrangements and a sophisticated orchestra would make Robert Pattinson's 007 entrance feel like a spectacle.

Versión en español: README.es.md.

Find the network fault in seconds, not hours. Upload a .pcap / .pcapng capture (gzip too) and PcapAnalyzer tells you what is failing, why, and what to check next. It runs on your own machine, so captures never leave your network.

According to recent reports, free and open source (Apache 2.0). Status: beta.

You need Docker with Docker Compose. On Windows, run the script from Git Bash or WSL.

The script creates a random access token (shown once, stored in .env) and starts the app. When the build finishes, open http://localhost:8080, paste the token into the "API token" field (top right) and upload a capture, or click "Try the sample capture".

The app listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Do not expose it on a network without an authenticated reverse proxy: the API can use your AI account. QUICKSTART.md has the details, the AI setup and troubleshooting.

You need Python 3.9+, Node 20+ and tshark (installed with Wireshark).

Sources indicate that open http://localhost:5173 and paste the same token. If tshark is not on your PATH, set TSHARK_PATH to the binary.

PcapAnalyzer is a beta. It has been tested with synthetic fixtures and public sample captures, and the most useful feedback is a capture where it misses a problem or reports one that is not real. Please open an problem at https://github.com/sebaandrada-cell/PcapAnalyzer/issues and describe the case. Do not attach captures that contain real credentials or customer data; anonymise them first or describe the pattern.

The technical reference (JSON schema, detector thresholds, limits, API errors) is in README.es.md, in Spanish.

Apache License 2.0. See NOTICE for third-party software: tshark / Wireshark (GPL) runs as a separate program and is not distributed with PcapAnalyzer.

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, presently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Industry observers note that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

Sources indicate that it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple indicates the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

It has been revealed that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

According to recent reports, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Industry News: 10 Fantasy Shows That Are Perfect Replacements for 'Game of Thrones'

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that game of Thrones was, to put it mildly, a cultural phenomenon.
  • The series was popular for its romantic and political themes, its massive scale, action sequences, and its memorable cast of characters.
  • Recent findings suggest that legend of the Seeker is a show that was not received well by critics, but was appreciated more by fans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that game of Thrones was, to put it mildly, a cultural phenomenon. It's nearly impossible to describe how huge this show really was in the world of television. Based on the novels by George R. R. Martin, the show ran for eight seasons before concluding, ushering in a new era of fantasy TV, where the genre has become more popular than ever.

The series was popular for its romantic and political themes, its massive scale, action sequences, and its memorable cast of characters. Since its conclusion in 2019, however, many fans have been left feeling unsatisfied, especially given how many fans were disappointed by its conclusion. If this sounds like you, you may wish to check out these shows like Game of Thrones, which can offer some relief, if not total temporary replacement.

Recent findings suggest that legend of the Seeker is a show that was not received well by critics, but was appreciated more by fans. Granted, it is not a perfect show; heck, it isn't even a great one. However, it might be just the thing to replace Game of Thrones for those who need a fantasy series to binge. The show is based on the novels by Terry Goodkind, who has always been a controversial figure, which is likely why the show was badly reviewed or barely acknowledged.

The show follows the life of a young man as he begins seeking revenge following the murder of his father, which unravels conspiracies and reveals secrets. The series was canceled after two seasons, which may have been the right call due to its reception and revenue. Regardless, it's enjoyable enough for some fantasy fans, meaning those who miss Thrones may find some solace in this one.

The Shannara Chronicles is an underrated little gem based on the novels by Terry Brooks. The series of novels is widely considered one of the most defining works of fantasy, though the show never lived up to this reputation. It's not bad whatsoever; it just wasn't super popular upon release. Set in the distant future, after an apocalyptic event has reduced humanity back to the Middle Ages, the story is about a half-human/half-elf on a quest to prevent a magical tree from dying and releasing a horde of demons.

The show stars Austin Butler as the protagonist, Wil, before he became as popular as he is now. As fun as the show is, the fact that it got cut short is a major turnoff for a lot of fantasy fans. However, if you're looking for a series with a complex, layered, and magical world, while also being based on a beloved novel series, The Shannara Chronicles might just be the series for you.

In a recent development, xena: Warrior Princess is actually a spin-off of another series, yet it became wildly more successful than its predecessor. Today, it is considered a cult series, which is constantly being rediscovered by eager fans. The show is set in Ancient Greece, in the First Century BCE. The principal actor is Lucy Lawless, who plays the eponymous Xena. Xena is a completely original character that does not appear in real Greek mythology, yet the way she is written allows her to seamlessly integrate.

According to recent reports, though much of the show is about Xena and her doing battle with various monsters from Greek myth, politics and romance do play a major part in the story. Namely, in the way that Xena attempts to prevent the Roman Republic, under the reign of Julius Caesar, from expanding too far into Greece. It's not as mature or violent as Thrones, but it's still a superb series and a staple of the '90s that is perfect for filling the void that Thrones left behind.

Unlike a lot of the other shows on this list, Outlander is actually a low fantasy. What this means is that it is set on Earth, throughout various points in history, rather than a fabricated, secondary world. It opens in the years following World War II, when a former nurse is magically sent back in time, arriving in the 18th Century. Here, she meets a Scottish Highland warrior whom she falls in love with. Across the show's various seasons, the two star-crossed lovers move through various periods in history.

In a recent development, based on a novel series by Diana Gabaldon, Outlander is, at heart, a romantasy TV show, which can turn a lot of people off. However, it does share a lot of common themes with Game of Thrones. For one, it's actually quite action-packed and features a lot of politics and feuding nobles. And of course, it's chock-full of steamy romance, including sex scenes, which, let's face it, is one of the main reasons Thrones sold so well.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power got off to an admittedly rough start. Based on the enormous legendarium crafted by groundbreaking fantasy author J. R. R. Tolkien, the series is an almost entirely original story using familiar characters. It exists as a separate entity from Peter Jackson's master-crafted film trilogy, and was meant to serve as the flagship fantasy series for Amazon Prime Video.

According to recent reports, however, three seasons in, it finally seems to be hitting its stride. Fans and critics alike were much more receptive to this new season, even those who were harsher on the previous two. For those missing Game of Thrones, The Rings of Power provides a similar sprawling, lore-heavy, high fantasy world, political drama, large-scale battles, and a cast of memorable characters.

According to recent reports, the Witcher got off on the right foot, but has been kind of dragging itself down lately. Based on the beloved novels by Andrzej Sapkowski, The Witcher is about a professional monster hunter called a Witcher, who roams around a high fantasy world searching for contracts to make his living. Along the way, he meets numerous enemies and allies, and even establishes himself in some high courts.

This is definitely a dark fantasy show, with all of the cynicism that Game of Thrones bears. Most of the beasts and beings featured in the show are all pulled straight from folklore and mythology from cultures around the world, making for a fascinating mish-mash of magic. This show came out at exactly the right time, just months after Thrones ended, and was the perfect replacement that a lot of people needed. For a time, at least.

It has been revealed that the Wheel of Time is based on a series of 15 novels by the late author Robert Jordan. The series is set thousands of years in Earth's future, where a tired age is concluding. As the world prepares for armageddon, the search begins for the Chosen One known as the Dragon Reborn, who is destined to either save the world from its destruction, or to destroy it himself.

The show got off to a rocky start, but each season proved better than the one before it, culminating in the excellent third season. Why Amazon Prime decided to cancel it at this point remains mystifying. Regardless, the show is full of politics, romance, and massive battle sequences. Though it developed its own distinct identity and style from Game of Thrones, the two share a lot of similar tropes.

Netflix's Kingdom is a South Korean fantasy/horror series that's about as close to Thrones as you can get. Set in the historic kingdom of Joseon at the turn of the 17th Century, the story centres on a beleaguered prince who desperately tries to hold onto his throne as a rival clan tries to usurp it from him. In the process, the rival Haewon Cho family uses a mythical resurrection plant to unleash a zombie horde.

Based on a webtoon turned graphic novel, Kingdom has all the hallmarks that Thrones did: large-scale battles, an army of the undead, feuding royals, romance, and a cast of colourful characters. It really is one of the most perfect replacements you can find, even if it is low fantasy rather than high fantasy. Sadly, the show was soft-cancelled by Netflix after two seasons and one special episode.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is the second spin-off series from the Game of Thrones universe. It is set 100 years prior to Thrones, though it operates on a much smaller scale. The story is based on the novellas written by George R. R. Martin, colloquially dubbed "Dunk and Egg" by fans. The show follows a hedge knight and his trusty young squire as they travel across the land of Westeros, never quite fitting in wherever they go.

As mentioned, the scale of this show is substantially smaller. It's not necessarily about politics or huge battles, and is more of a traveller's tale with heavy elements of comedy. It's still action-packed, to be sure, albeit these fights are much more about one-on-one scraps rather than clashes of armies. Regardless, it's a perfect return to form for the universe, and an excellent show in general.

House of the Dragon is the first spin-off of Game of Thrones, which is set centuries prior to the original series. Industry observers note that specifically, the show is about the Targaryen clan and their rise to power; how they conquered Westeros and united the Seven Kingdoms under one banner, albeit not without their fair share of adversaries. It allows fans of Thrones to examine the inner workings of a nearly extinct family from the original, while also providing the closest experience to Thrones as possible.

UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….
  • The story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….

The story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Recent findings suggest that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

Sources indicate that in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

It has been revealed that this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve mentioned many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the company found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple unveiled it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to latest people and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have mentioned many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

According to recent reports, at this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal mentioned. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it debuted – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

#85915. Breaking: My monitor was cutting my download speed by 75%

📅 2026-11-15 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1544 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tymscar ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: My monitor was cutting my download speed by 75%

📅 2026-11-15 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tymscar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow I am one of those few very lucky people to have the opportunity of owning a 2.5 gig symmetrical line for my internet.
  • It’s run by this one guy (Hey Keith!), and I know I can always message them and they respond promptly, as they did this time.
  • I didn’t have time for debugging, because I needed to travel 2000 km to the other side of the continent for a family emergency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow I am one of those few very lucky people to have the opportunity of owning a 2.5 gig symmetrical line for my internet. But one day, when I wanted to brag to my equally nerdy friends, shock and horror: 600 Mbps down? Luckily my upload speed was still 2.4 Gbps, so I didn’t lose all my bragging rights, but that’s weird, right? If anything, you’d expect the opposite!

My ISP is pretty cool. It’s run by this one guy (Hey Keith!), and I know I can always message them and they respond promptly, as they did this time. We tried to run through a few debugging steps, they checked on their end, and everything was normal. I tried my work laptop too, same speed.

I didn’t have time for debugging, because I needed to travel 2000 km to the other side of the continent for a family emergency.

But as soon as I got back, I got curious again. What could it be? In retrospect, I now know when it started: when I moved all my connections onto my Studio Display XDR. I wanted to have a one-cable setup, and the monitor offered me that. I’ve had it for half a year now, and I don’t think I’ve ever run a speed test through it. 600 Mbps was more than fast enough for me to never realise I wasn’t getting three quarters of the speed I was paying for 🤦.

Pings to other wired computers during a download would fail 10% of the time over Ethernet through the adapter plugged into my screen, and 0% of the time over Wi-Fi. What made it stranger was that there were no dropped frame errors in macOS’s logs at all. This was the substantial hint for me: the adapter was dropping them before the computer could know.

In a recent development, I then plugged the adapter straight into my Mac instead of the monitor, and ran an iperf3 server on my UDR 7: 2.3 Gbps. So the cable, the router and the adapter are all fine? What about fast.com? Perfect speeds there too! 2.2 down and 2.3 up when connected straight in. As soon as I connected it to the display, it was back to 600 down again.

So it’s the display, right? Well, I would find out: sort of yes, sort of no, which is why I wanted to write this blog post. I couldn’t find anything online explaining the exact cause, and it’s quite a cool reason.

It has been revealed that the adapter uses a Realtek RTL8156B, which on macOS binds to Apple’s generic USB networking driver. But Realtek ship their own driver on their website, so I thought I’d give that a go! I installed it and, to my surprise, it almost doubled the download speed to 1.1 Gbps, but that was still nowhere close to 2.5. First hint that it couldn’t just be the monitor’s fault.

In a recent development, then I tried flow control. I had never truly looked into this before, and I think it’s quite neat to know about if you were also ignorant of it like me. Basically, when a device receives Ethernet frames it can’t keep up with, it just drops them. With flow control (it’s something your router or switch has to support), it can send the sender a “pause” frame, and the sender then buffers the data on its side, instead of the receiver (the adapter in this case) on its side. I turned it on in my UniFi console and guess what, download jumped to around 2 Gbps, with upload still at full speed! Yay! Well, not so fast….

Sources indicate that I don’t like it always being on, because it can add latency to other systems like my gaming PC. Can you work around it? For sure, you can disable it on those computers, but it’s janky, and it’s another thing I need to remember when my Sauerbraten game starts lagging. I need fewer things to remember, considering I am 30 in a couple of months. My memory is not what it used to be.

In a recent development, yeah, isn’t that weird? First of all, it looks like the port can indeed do 2.5 in both directions. I already knew that, because I get much more than that from my external SSD through the monitor’s Thunderbolt port. So the problem is not the monitor again? But it has to be!

Well, I had another idea. How about I connect to my Linux box, which is also on 2.5, and send perfectly smooth UDP traffic at a fixed rate with flow control off? Then I can check the chip’s own counter of dropped frames:.

In a recent development, so basically no drops whatsoever when connected straight to my Mac, but loads of drops after about 168k frames per second (roughly 2 Gbps). Remember that number. That number comes from the adapter’s own counters: however much I sent, the number of frames it managed to hand over to the Mac each second flattened out at about 168,000, and everything above that was dropped.

In a recent development, why did this not happen on my SSD? What was the only difference I could find? Bursts!

Recent findings suggest that when the Mac reads data from a USB 3 device, the device sends some packets, then has to wait for the Mac to say “lgtm, send more!”. The SSD enclosure sends 16 packets before needing a go-ahead message back. The RTL8156B in my Ethernet adapter sends 4.

In a recent development, here is a diagram of my best understanding of why this is an problem. I made this diagram 100 times, and I think I can probably improve it more, but if it helps you understand the issue, I have done my job.

Sources indicate that as you can see, the speed of packets coming into the adapter is 2.5 Gbps. That’s what the router pushes in. The speed going out is around 2 Gbps. The reason is that if you add up the average time it takes to get the go-ahead through my monitor’s hub, which is around 7.6 µs, to the average time it takes to send 4 KB, around 8.2 µs, you can find what the maximum speed is.

Well, if the speed of the drain from my adapter to my Mac is half a gig slower than the speed of the input, then you can imagine the buffer getting filled more and more until it overflows. Those are dropped packets, which result in a hard backoff when the router resends them, so you drop loads in speed. And that’s the reason for all of this.

Industry observers note that I have a cupboard full of USB-C Ethernet adapters. Don’t ask.

The problem is they’re all 1 gig adapters, so any of the tests I made would not tell me anything, because the challenges don’t start at 1 gig. They start at around 2… If I run my 2.5 gig adapter at 1 gig speeds, I get 1 gig downloads with the official driver. If I run it at 1.5, I get 1.5. If I run it at 2, well, I get 1….

So I thought I would do what any human would do, and I spent more money on a new adapter. Another UGREEN, but this time it’s one that promises 5 Gbps and uses the RTL8157 chip instead: UGREEN 5G USB-C Ethernet adapter. My reasoning was that if this one could get me better speeds, it would help me understand how. And that it did!

With this adapter, I dropped 0 frames:.

It has been revealed that why? Well, looking through what each adapter tells me about itself:.

I can see that instead of sending 4 1 KB packets per burst, it would send 8! And the speed of the link was also 2x faster, so those 8 KB would go 2x faster to the Mac. That means the time spent was 8 times lower to send the same data, and while the wait for the go-ahead was identical, the theoretical speed from the adapter to the Mac, including the wait for the go-ahead, was a maximum of 4.5 Gbps. That’s much bigger than the 2.5 coming into the adapter, so the buffer would never fill up, packets would never drop and everything was great, even if the “go-ahead” response was still much slower than when connected directly to the Mac.

According to recent reports, I think the big takeaway from this is that all the things you think are quite easy to understand, such as transfer speeds, have so many cool intricacies that it’s worth diving deep every so often. Who would’ve thought that the speed of the link between the adapter and the Mac was defined not only by the link speed itself in Gbps, but also by the time it took your Mac to reply, by the amount of packets, by the speed of those packets, by the number of packets in a burst, and by the size of those packets?

See you next time, when I will spend just as much time on another trivial thing that we can all learn from!

Why Black Friday and Cyber Monday Are Bad Days to Impulse Buy Electronics

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1122 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.
  • Some Cyber Monday deals are still live, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Some Cyber Monday deals are still live, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Follow our live blog to stay up-to-date on the best sales we find.

Browse our editors’ picks for a curated list of our favorite sales on laptops, fitness tech, appliances, and more.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be said for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before newly introduced models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

Recent findings suggest that in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The problem isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Industry observers note that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a latest tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

It has been revealed that to avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

In a recent development, if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

It has been revealed that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Apple’s new HomeView just released last Friday, but some early adopters reported concerns with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems.

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the tech giant’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following issue:.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

In a recent development, it’s unknown how many reports of Siri concerns on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta owners. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

Sources indicate that with HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a new glitch you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now indicates: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

It has been revealed that if you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView revision, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

It’s understandable that issues might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, users might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

Microsoft To Do is retiring, including Mac and iOS apps

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • Sources indicate that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • In a recent development, “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what consumers need to know.

Sources indicate that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

In a recent development, “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

Sources indicate that on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no prepares for a native Mac app.

According to recent reports, you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

Industry observers note that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

“We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team intends. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.
